findings.title: CSP nonce never reaches Next.js's own scripts
findings.desc: Next.js extracts the nonce for its bootstrap/hydration `<script>` tags from the **incoming request's** `Content-Security-Policy` header, so the CSP must also be set on `requestHeaders` (as in Next's own docs), not just on the response. As written, Next's scripts are emitted without `nonce`, and because `'strict-dynamic'` causes `'self'` to be ignored in `script-src`, every script is blocked and the app fails to hydrate.

findings.title: Comment states a mechanism that doesn't exist
findings.desc: "Next.js automatically tags its own bootstrap `<script>` elements with the nonce from the response's CSP header" is wrong — Next reads the CSP from the request headers forwarded by the proxy; this incorrect assumption is what causes finding 1 and will mislead future maintainers debugging blocked scripts.

findings.title: Dev mode will break without `'unsafe-eval'`
findings.desc: Next.js's development server (HMR / Fast Refresh, React refresh runtime) uses `eval`, which this `script-src` forbids; a dev-only relaxation (`process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"`) is normally required or local development is unusable.

findings.title: `x-nonce` request header is dead code
findings.desc: The comment says layouts read `x-nonce` and pass it to `<Script>` tags, but no consumer exists (the layout explicitly declines to read it), so this header and its rationale are stale.

findings.title: `await headers()` in the root layout forces every route dynamic
findings.desc: Opting the root layout out of static rendering disables static generation and full-route caching for the entire app just to trigger the proxy; the proxy already runs on all matched requests, so this cost is only needed for pages that would otherwise be prerendered with a baked-in nonce.

2. app/layout.tsx:27-30 | Medium | misleading docs | Comment states a mechanism that doesn't exist | "Next.js automatically tags its own bootstrap `<script>` elements with the nonce from the response's CSP header" is wrong — Next reads the CSP from the request headers forwarded by the proxy; this incorrect assumption is what causes finding 1 and will mislead future maintainers debugging blocked scripts.
3. proxy.ts:21-31 | Medium | correctness | Dev mode will break without `'unsafe-eval'` | Next.js's development server (HMR / Fast Refresh, React refresh runtime) uses `eval`, which this `script-src` forbids; a dev-only relaxation (`process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"`) is normally required or local development is unusable.
4. proxy.ts:39-42 | Low | consistency | `x-nonce` request header is dead code | The comment says layouts read `x-nonce` and pass it to `<Script>` tags, but no consumer exists (the layout explicitly declines to read it), so this header and its rationale are stale.

findings.title: CSP not forwarded on request headers, so Next never nonces its scripts
findings.desc: Next.js extracts the nonce for its bootstrap/hydration `<script>` tags from the *incoming request's* `Content-Security-Policy` header, but this code sets CSP only on the response (`response.headers.set`) and puts just `x-nonce` on the forwarded request headers. Because `'strict-dynamic'` makes the `'self'` source expression ignored, every Next script will be un-nonced and blocked, breaking hydration/client interactivity; the CSP header value must also be `set` on `requestHeaders`.

findings.title: Comment misstates both the mechanism and the reason
findings.desc: Proxy/middleware runs on every request regardless of whether a route is statically rendered — the real reason to opt out is that a prerendered HTML document would carry a stale nonce; and the claim that Next tags scripts "from the response's CSP header" is wrong (it reads the request header), which is what leads to finding #1.

findings.title: Missing `'unsafe-eval'` for development will break dev HMR
findings.desc: Next dev builds (webpack `eval-source-map` and Turbopack HMR) execute code via `eval`/`new Function`; with `script-src` lacking `'unsafe-eval'` in dev, hot reload and dev overlay will be blocked. Consider branching on `process.env.NODE_ENV`.

findings.title: `x-nonce` request header is set but never consumed
findings.desc: The comment says layouts read it via `headers()` and pass it to `<Script>` tags, but `app/layout.tsx` explicitly does not read it, leaving dead state and a comment that contradicts the code.

findings.title: Matcher lookahead is prefix-based, not segment-based
findings.desc: `(?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico)` also excludes unrelated routes whose first segment merely starts with those strings (e.g. `/api-docs`, `/favicon.ico.txt`), silently dropping CSP for them; anchor with a trailing `/` or `$` (e.g. `api(?:/|$)`).

3. proxy.ts:22 | Medium | correctness | Missing `'unsafe-eval'` for development will break dev HMR | Next dev builds (webpack `eval-source-map` and Turbopack HMR) execute code via `eval`/`new Function`; with `script-src` lacking `'unsafe-eval'` in dev, hot reload and dev overlay will be blocked. 4. proxy.ts:39-40 | Low | API/consistency drift | `x-nonce` request header is set but never consumed | The comment says layouts read it via `headers()` and pass it to `<Script>` tags, but `app/layout.tsx` explicitly does not read it, leaving dead state and a comment that contradicts the code.

findings.title: Nonce never reaches Next.js renderer — all scripts blocked by `strict-dynamic`
findings.desc: Next.js extracts the render nonce by parsing the `content-security-policy` header off the *incoming request* headers (`app-render` reads `req.headers['content-security-policy']`), not off the response. Since only `x-nonce` is forwarded on the request and nothing reads it, Next's bootstrap `<script>` tags get no `nonce` attribute; because `'strict-dynamic'` causes `'self'` to be ignored, every Next script is blocked and the app never hydrates. Fix by also doing `requestHeaders.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp)`.

findings.title: Comment misstates how Next.js obtains the nonce
findings.desc: "Next.js automatically tags its own bootstrap `<script>` elements with the nonce from the response's CSP header" is wrong — the nonce is read from the request-side CSP header, which this diff never sets; the comment hides the bug in #1.

findings.title: Dev mode breaks: no `'unsafe-eval'` / `blob:` worker allowance
findings.desc: Next.js dev builds use `eval`-based source maps and React Refresh, so `script-src` without `'unsafe-eval'` (typically gated on `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`) will make `next dev` unusable; `default-src 'self'` also blocks `blob:` workers if any are used.

findings.title: `await headers()` in root layout forces every route dynamic
findings.desc: Calling `headers()` in the root layout opts the entire app out of static generation and the full route cache, which is a site-wide rendering/perf regression; a per-request CSP header can instead be attached without disabling static rendering (or scoped to routes that actually need the nonce).

findings.title: `x-nonce` is set but never consumed; comment describes behavior that doesn't exist
findings.desc: No layout or component reads `x-nonce`, and the layout comment explicitly says it doesn't need to — leaving a header whose stated purpose ("so layouts can read it and pass it to `<Script>` tags") is unimplemented.

findings.title: Matcher regex over-excludes and drops CSP on prefetches
findings.desc: `(?!api|_next/static|...)` is a prefix, not path-segment, match, so routes like `/apidocs` or `/favicon.icon` silently lose CSP; likewise all `next-router-prefetch`/`purpose: prefetch` responses ship with no CSP header at all.
